subject: Re: Zenrupt capacity plan — staggered burst slabs & eviction rules
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@zenrupt.com>
To: ava.chen@redwood.com
Cc: infra@zenrupt.com
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial sizing ask: predictable burst for Q2 pilot

Hi Ava,

Quick note from the infra team — we're about to kick off a month-long pilot for our generative search feature and need guidance on Dedicated capacity sizing. Expected steady-state is ~150 concurrent inference workers at p99 token latency <= 120ms, but we want a predictable burst buffer up to 2.5x for marketing demos (short bursts of 10–20 minutes).

Questions we need answered before procurement signs off:
- Can Redwood provide a "staggered burst slab" approach so we reserve a small committed pool and allow short preemptible bursts?
- How are eviction/preemption rules enforced (granularity, per-customer fairness)?
- Price model for burst minutes versus reserved capacity — any credits or pro-rated billing?
- What telemetry will we get to monitor when bursts occur and which requests were evicted/fell back to hosted?

We can share logs and peak histograms if that helps model the headroom. Attaching our preliminary concurrency histogram.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Platform Engineering, Zenrupt

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@zenrupt.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial sizing ask: predictable burst for Q2 pilot

Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the histogram, that helps a lot. High level answer: yes, we can do a staggered burst slab with a small committed pool + short-duration preemptible capacity. I'll outline a concrete proposal below and attach a capacity model for you to poke at (zr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx).

Proposal (summary):
- Committed slab: sized for 1.2x of your steady-state (-> cover typical load and 20% cushion).
- Staggered burst slabs: two tiers — Tier A (non-preemptible, short-term 30m increments) sized for 1.5x for scheduled demos; Tier B (preemptible, up to additional 2.5x) with eviction windows and soft-fallthrough to hosted API.
- Eviction rules: preemptible Tier B uses fair-share across preemptible tenants and respects per-job minimum runtime (60s) to avoid mid-token kills. Evictions are signaled via 503 with retry hints; we provide request-level trace ids so you can correlate in your telemetry.
- Billing: committed capacity billed monthly as usual. Tier A billed as reserved short-term increments at a discounted minute-rate. Tier B billed at a higher per-minute rate but with burst credits: we can include 5000 free burst-minutes per month for the pilot as a one-time concession.
- Observability: Console dashboard will expose per-route burst minutes, eviction counts (per minute), fallbacks to hosted, and per-customer preemption latency impact. We'll also provide a CSV export and a short webhook for real-time alerts.

Next steps: Diego and Aditya from our capacity team have a couple of follow-up asks (attached) so they can finalize the sizing sheet. Can we schedule a quick 30m sync tomorrow to run the numbers against your histogram? Also, please confirm whether you need burst-only in us-west or multi-region.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
To: ava.chen@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 08:49:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL — quick clarifications for Zenrupt slab simulation

Ava / Aditya — looping you in with the model notes. From Maya's histogram the 99th percentile session length is ~18s but there are demo spikes with 10–20 minute sustained concurrency increases. Our conservative approach: size committed for 1.2x and Tier A at 1.5x (scheduled). Tier B (preemptible) should be time-limited to 20 minutes continuous per tenant to avoid noisy neighbor long bursts.

Model assumptions to confirm with Zenrupt:
- Typical token length and average tokens/sec (we need to estimate GPU occupancy).
- Acceptable preemption policy: backoff hints vs immediate retry.
- Whether certain routes (auth/health/checks) must never be preempted.

I attached the eviction matrix and a recommended allocation algorithm (sla_eviction_matrix.pdf). If they accept the 5000 pilot burst-minutes credit we can also soften the billing on Tier B.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, ava.chen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL — price calc and DocuSign items

Diego / Ava — ran the cost sim in zr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx using their histogram; outputs:
- Committed pool (1.2x steady-state): 24 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day -> monthly committed=~720 GPU-hours.
- Tier A scheduled burst (1.5x): ~120 minutes/day peak buffer -> priced as reserved increments at 60% of on-demand minute-rate.
- Tier B preemptible: priced at 1.8x on-demand minute-rate but with first 5k minutes free for pilot.

DocuSign / contract items that need explicit language:
- Definition of "preemption" and minimal grace period (we propose 60s).
- Billing rounding rules for minute increments.
- SLA for overflow fallback to hosted API (response time goal) and mapping to credits.

I added a short summary we can send back to Zenrupt and uploaded the draft SOW link: https://hub.redwood.example/records/DEAL-2026-1198

Aditya

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@zenrupt.com>
Cc: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, infra@zenrupt.com
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 16:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Zenrupt capacity plan — staggered burst slabs & eviction rules

Maya — thanks again for the histogram and patience while we modeled options. Short version: we can deliver the staggered slab plan you requested. Attached are three artifacts: zr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx (detailed sim), sla_eviction_matrix.pdf (eviction rules + fairness algorithm), and a short policy summary (redwood-burst-policy-summary.docx).

Key points we agreed internally and recommend for the pilot:
- Committed pool = 1.2x steady-state (covers normal traffic)
- Tier A (scheduled) = capacity for short, booked demos — reserved in 30m increments at a discounted rate
- Tier B (preemptible) = additional headroom up to 2.5x with a 20-minute continuous cap and a 60s grace period on preemption; evictions will be signaled and requests will fall back to Redwood hosted API if enabled in your account
- Pilot concession: 5,000 free Tier B burst-minutes for the first 30 days.

Action items:
1) Confirm region (us-west) and whether you want hosted fallback enabled for demo traffic by EOD Wed 11 Feb.
2) If yes, we'll send a short SOW and DocuSign link (see https://docusign.example.com/tx/5f8a2b).
3) I'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with Diego and Aditya to step through zr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx and lock numbers.

If helpful I can also turn on a real-time webhook that posts eviction events to your Slack channel during the pilot.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
